name: mcp-server-compute
title: MCP Server (Compute)
description: Add a user-scoped MCP server to your product, running on Supabase Compute.

files.content:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2023"],
    "module": "nodenext",
    "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["main.ts", "tools/**/*.ts"]
}

# A Compute instance receives its configuration as environment variables. Copy
# this file and set the values as project secrets before pushing:
#   cp supabase/compute/mcp-server/.env.example supabase/compute/mcp-server/.env
#   supabase secrets set --env-file supabase/compute/mcp-server/.env
#   npm run build --prefix supabase/compute/mcp-server
#   supabase compute push mcp-server --project-ref <project-ref>

# Required. The project URL and a publishable key, the same values passed to
# createClient(). Unlike an Edge Function, a Compute instance is not given
# these automatically.
SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-ref.supabase.co
SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=your-publishable-key

# Must match [compute.<name>] in supabase/config.toml. It is the last segment
# of this service's public URL, so the advertised OAuth resource identifier
# depends on it.
MCP_COMPUTE_SERVICE_NAME=mcp-server

# Optional. Set only when clients reach this service somewhere other than
# SUPABASE_URL + /compute/v1/<name>, for example behind a custom domain. It
# must be the exact URL clients call, which RFC 9728 requires to match.
# MCP_RESOURCE_SERVER=https://mcp.example.com

# Optional. A third-party OAuth 2.1 issuer for external clients. Unset, this
# project's Supabase Auth is the authorization server.
# MCP_AUTHORIZATION_SERVER=https://example.clerk.accounts.dev

# Keep the protocol-level server name short and project-specific.
MCP_SERVER_NAME=supabase-mcp
MCP_SERVER_DESCRIPTION="MCP access to this Supabase project for the signed-in user."

docs: Set `[compute.mcp-server]` in `supabase/config.toml` with `runtime = "node"` and `source = "supabase/compute/mcp-server/dist"`. The block ships sources and a build script, not a build: run `npm install` then `npm run build` in `supabase/compute/mcp-server` to write `dist/index.mjs`, a single ESM bundle with its dependencies inlined, then `supabase compute push mcp-server --project-ref <ref>` (or `npm run deploy -- --project-ref <ref>`, which does both). Nothing is installed server-side and the `source` directory is uploaded as-is, so the bundle is what removes the need for a vendored `node_modules`. Build on every machine that pushes: `dist`, `node_modules` and `.env` are git-ignored. Set `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` as secrets: a Compute instance is not given them automatically. A trusted product backend can call it with the signed-in user's access token. For external clients, install the [OAuth Consent block](https://supabase.com/library/docs/nextjs/oauth-consent), enable OAuth and dynamic registration, and set the Auth Site URL to the consent app. Every call runs through the user's RLS-scoped client. OAuth tokens include `client_id`; product sessions do not, so define policies for both paths. See [MCP authentication](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/mcp-authentication) and [token security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/token-security).
